added.criterion: For every explicitly supplied PHP-FPM worker PID, the scanner and worker have identical effective UID/GID/groups, zero effective/permitted/ambient capabilities, matching project tree, mount namespace and Linux security context. Kernel access observations find no writable object or replaceable code root in the complete bounded configured app/vendor/lib inventory. Unsupported identity, seccomp, links or inventory gaps remain UNKNOWN.

Within the complete bounded configured upload path inventory, readable files contain no explicit long PHP opening tags or configured htaccess script-handler signatures and no PHP-like executable filename extension. Missing/unreadable/oversized eligible files, unfollowed links and traversal-budget gaps remain UNKNOWN. This is a signature policy, not absence of arbitrary executable content or prevention of server execution.

In a nonempty bounded deployed authorization_role inventory and complete bounded authorization_rule inventory, every direct allow rule for Magento_Backend::all or Magento_Adminhtml::all assigned to a group role has a role ID in the explicitly configured approved_role_ids policy. Missing policy, malformed/orphan rows, direct user grants or incomplete tables remain UNKNOWN. This checks direct stored grants, not inherited effective privileges or business least privilege.

The supplied checkout path returns a successful same-origin no-redirect HTTPS GET with one unambiguous enforced Content-Security-Policy. The emitted policy explicitly defines script-src, connect-src, frame-src, form-action, object-src and base-uri; assessed sources contain no wildcard, unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval or broad scheme-only source. object-src is exactly none, base-uri is exactly none or self, and reporting is present when configured. Report-only alone fails; redirect/inaccessible checkout, multiple policies, unsupported syntax or incomplete collection remain UNKNOWN.

One successful same-origin no-redirect HTTPS GET at the configured path emits exactly one X-Content-Type-Options header whose trimmed value is nosniff. Missing or invalid header on an observed successful response fails; duplicate headers, redirects, transport failures and incomplete collection remain UNKNOWN. HSTS and frame protection are assessed separately.

Every explicitly configured integration debug/verbose setting path resolves through deployed env.php/config.php/default core_config_data or supported installed-module defaults to a recognized disabled value in default scope. Any recognized enabled value fails; omitted paths, missing values or unsupported flag representations remain UNKNOWN. This verifies named settings, not every third-party integration or store scope.

Every package in the readable bounded collected composer.lock inventory has source and/or dist URL and nonempty reference matching the supplied exact per-package source policy; replacement declarations and root composer.json repository declarations also match the supplied policy. Explicit metadata-only metapackages may have no source/dist. Missing package policies or incomplete source identity are unresolved. This compares collected declarations and does not verify installed bytes, canonical upstream truth or absence of malicious approved revisions.

The bounded readable schema-version-1 mitigation record inventory has a valid generated_at timestamp within configured max_age_days and covers each identity in the supplied nonempty expected_ids policy with a unique record containing nonempty advisory, package, version, owner, action, rollback and a valid future expires_at. This checks declared record structure and expiry only, not whether all deployed mitigations are declared, effective or approved.

Every explicitly inventoried Linux PHP-FPM worker is bound to its pool, executable identity and exact process start_ticks before and after a complete bounded nonempty /proc process-map observation. No Xdebug-named shared module is mapped in these verified workers. Missing or changed identity, empty/unreadable/truncated maps or malformed inventory remain UNKNOWN. This observes configured process mappings at scan time, not every deployment worker, Xdebug feature mode, statically linked code or complete PHP runtime settings.
